title: Machine learning and peptide-array experiments reveal new substrates for protein-modifying enzymes
summary: A hybrid workflow coupled machine-learning models with enzyme-treated peptide arrays to predict previously unexplored protein post-translational-modification sites. Experimental validation confirmed 37–43% of proposed sites across SET8 and SIRT1–7; mass spectrometry confirmed dynamic methylation for several SET8 substrates and deacetylation at 64 unique SIRT2 sites. The work also found altered SET8 substrate networks associated with breast-cancer missense mutations.
ai_technology: Enzyme-specific ML-hybrid substrate prediction models trained from high-throughput peptide-array assays
organization: Carleton University; Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

evidence.tested: Experimental validation confirmed 37–43% of proposed sites across SET8 and SIRT1–7; mass spectrometry confirmed dynamic methylation for several SET8 substrates and deacetylation at 64 unique SIRT2 sites.
evidence.unknown: Reported validation rate is 37–43% of proposed sites, so predictions are not uniformly confirmed. Results concern in-vitro enzyme assays and selected sites; disease relevance of the altered SET8 network is not established as a clinical mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Learned enzyme-specific substrate preferences from experimental array measurements and prioritized novel PTM sites for experimental follow-up; this enabled the reported new SET8/SIRT substrate assignments.
